description: The O-RAN Software Community (O-RAN SC) develops open-source software for the radio access network (RAN) that follows the architecture specified by the O-RAN ALLIANCE. It was created by the O-RAN ALLIANCE and the Linux Foundation and during 2026 was folded into Linux Foundation Networking (LFN). Coverage: the software is generic and used worldwide in labs and testbeds. Named releases (the latest is the M release) bundle the near-real-time RAN Intelligent Controller and its xApp framework, the non-real-time RIC and rApps, the service management and orchestration layer, O-DU and O-RU simulators, and integration and testing tooling aligned with 3GPP. Format and access: source code in the project's Gerrit and GitHub mirrors, container images and Helm charts, with release notes and documentation on the project wiki; free. Licence: mainly Apache 2.0, with some components under other open-source terms, and the site under Linux Foundation terms of use. Caveats: components are research-grade and change between releases, full deployments need Kubernetes and radio hardware or simulators, and not every component is maintained in every release. Simulation uses: building open RAN testbeds and digital twins of mobile networks, and testing RIC control applications for capacity planning and resilience of cells and slices. Related records: ns-3 (platform-ns-3) and the OpenAirInterface RF simulator (model-openairinterface-rf-simulator) are simulators often coupled with O-RAN SC components.
